tasks.short: Check order completeness and route missing information for follow-up.

steps.what: Gather the order draft and its supporting customer documents.
Compare customer documents with the draft's customer details, items, quantities and delivery instructions.

loop.input: Order review pack, customer record and product catalogue.
loop.output: Field differences with source references and unresolved item matches.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, units and quantities; require source references and flag ambiguous matches.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair attempt; unresolved differences go to the order clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer documents contain varied wording and layouts; structured orders bypass the model.

steps.what: Check required fields and record missing or inconsistent information.
Ask the customer or account representative to clarify incomplete order details.
Assign the order to the appropriate processing or clarification queue.

tasks.design: An integration assembles each order review pack from the {EMAIL}, {DOCS} and {ERP}. A bounded comparison loop flags document differences; configured rules in the {ERP} check completeness and route orders. The {WORKFLOW} prepares field-specific clarification requests for the order clerk to approve before sending through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Required fields were often enforceable, but customer attachments, inconsistent item descriptions and disconnected queues still required manual comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation features cover structured checks. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records, while bounded document comparison handles variable wording.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting specifications, poor customer records and unclear responsibility for answering queries still need people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparently complete order still expresses an unclear or impractical customer requirement.

ambition.what: Review recurring missing-field causes weekly with the sales supervisor.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from checking every field to resolving conflicting instructions and recurring intake problems. The clerk can propose intake changes; approval of commercial exceptions stays with the authorised role.

reach.task: Reduce order delays caused by incomplete customer instructions.
reach.learn: Group clarification reasons and distinguish intake defects from product or commercial questions.

evidence.claim: Document order capture can check customer, stock and price rules, route exceptions and post orders.
A vendor case reports 70% touchless orders; this does not establish this task's local saving.
Required-field checks and queue routing usually need rules rather than autonomous agents.

assumptions: The company uses the {ERP} for order drafts and receives some customer documents through the {EMAIL}.
Existing {ERP} configuration supports required fields and order statuses.
Step shares are estimates of today's task time, not measured savings.
GDPR controls cover customer documents, access, retention and any model processing.
unknowns: Required fields by order type and which rules already exist in the {ERP}.
Share of structured orders versus document orders.
Frequency of ambiguous item references and conflicting instructions.
Available interfaces and permissions.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed workflow changes.
research_questions: Which missing fields account for most clarification cycles?
Can native {ERP} configuration cover validation and routing before custom code is considered?
How accurately does document comparison detect consequential differences on representative historical orders?
new_work: Review ambiguous document comparisons and outbound clarification requests.
Maintain field requirements, queue rules and customer reference mappings.
Monitor integration failures and repeated clarification loops.
Arrange applicable employee consultation under national rules before rollout.

tasks.short: Collect customer and item details and create an order draft.

steps.what: Receive the customer's order request and supporting information.
Find the customer account and check stored addresses and billing details.
Contact the customer for missing addresses, billing references or item specifications.
Enter customer details, product numbers, quantities and specifications into the order form.

loop.input: Customer order text or attachment, confirmed customer details and product catalogue.
loop.output: Order draft with field provenance and unresolved values.
loop.check: Validate schema, exact customer and item identifiers, units and quantities; never invent missing values.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unresolved fields go to the order clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Unstructured requests need interpretation; structured form submissions use direct field mapping.

steps.what: Save the order draft and submit it for completeness review.

tasks.design: A configured intake form in the {WORKFLOW} collects missing factual details and reuses verified customer data from the {ERP}. An integration captures requests from the {EMAIL}; a bounded extraction loop prepares document orders for review, while structured submissions map directly into order drafts. The {ERP} queues saved drafts for completeness checking without releasing them for fulfilment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customers used different channels and formats, so clerks joined account records to free-text requests by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms and native imports already handle structured data. AI-assisted coding makes channel connections cheaper, and bounded extraction covers remaining document inputs.
tasks.still_hard: New customer identities, disputed billing changes and bespoke specifications require verification and conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a mistaken identity or specification before it becomes a confidently recorded order.

ambition.what: Provide a reusable repeat-order form for customers without electronic ordering connections.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time transcribing details and more time resolving account and specification exceptions. They gain no automatic right to change billing master data or accept unusual commercial terms.

reach.task: Create accurate customer accounts without duplicate records.
reach.learn: Customer matching, address validation and the evidence required for billing-detail changes.

evidence.claim: Order document capture can validate extracted information and post to the finance system.
Existing order software imports webshop orders and synchronises stock.
Validated forms and exact account matching can remove routine requests for missing factual details.

assumptions: The described intake route is email-led; phone requests remain an assisted alternative.
Standard factual questions can move to a customer form; inaccessible or ambiguous cases return to a person.
Billing information means invoice details and references; payment credentials use an approved payment channel.
An unmatched customer never triggers automatic account creation or a billing master-data change.
GDPR data minimisation, access control and retention apply to contact and billing details.
unknowns: Actual order-channel mix and customers' ability to use forms.
Customer identifiers available for reliable matching.
Verification policy for new accounts and billing-address changes.
Whether the {ERP} exposes draft-order interfaces and configurable forms.
Access approvals and employee consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Which repeated order details could be prefilled from verified records?
Which requests require a conversation even after structured intake?
Does native import support preserve customer specifications and source references?
new_work: Handle customers who cannot complete the form.
Review extracted fields and unresolved account matches.
Maintain form fields, catalogue mappings and duplicate-detection rules.
Resolve failed imports and reconcile duplicate submissions.
Complete access reviews and applicable employee consultation.

tasks.short: Recommend suitable merchandise or services after understanding the customer's needs.

steps.what: Discuss the customer's intended use, constraints, preferences and budget.
Look up product specifications, service terms, prices and availability.
Compare suitable options and select a recommendation with relevant trade-offs.

loop.input: Customer needs and options already filtered against explicit constraints.
loop.output: Short recommendation brief with trade-offs, source references and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Recheck hard constraints and current prices; the clerk verifies suitability and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; uncertain suitability goes to a sales specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Needs and trade-offs are expressed in free text; fixed filters alone cannot explain their fit.

steps.what: Explain the recommendation, answer concerns and agree the customer's next step.
Record the recommended option and agreed next step.

tasks.design: A deterministic lookup combines catalogue, price and availability data from the {ERP} with approved guidance in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares a sourced comparison for the clerk, who conducts the customer conversation. A configured template in the {CRM} records the selected option and next step after the clerk confirms them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information retrieval and recommendation judgement were mixed together, making the whole conversation appear resistant to automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Connected catalogue searches remove much of the lookup work. A bounded drafting loop can explain options using retrieved facts without taking over the customer discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Unspoken needs, technical compatibility, unreliable availability and consequential recommendations still require experience or specialist advice.
tasks.human_edge: Discovering what the customer actually needs and knowing when to challenge their initial request.

ambition.what: Offer structured option comparisons to occasional customers without a dedicated account representative.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more of the week discussing needs and trade-offs, with less catalogue searching. With training and explicit delegation, they can handle standard option comparisons while escalating technical and commercial exceptions.

reach.task: Assess compatibility for technically demanding customer requirements.
reach.learn: Recognise compatibility limits, capture intended use and identify when specialist validation is necessary.

reach.task: Follow up a recommendation with a suitable commercial offer.
reach.learn: Capture buying constraints and a useful next step without treating interest as a commitment.

evidence.claim: A shopping assistant for product advice exists; this does not prove suitability for technical recommendations.
An assistant study found higher support productivity, with larger gains for novices; recommendation quality needs separate testing.
Hard product constraints can be filtered deterministically before drafting an explanation.

assumptions: Current product facts and approved service terms are available from governed sources.
The clerk confirms outcome fields after the conversation; automatic call recording is unnecessary.
Recommendations stay within the clerk's existing competence and commercial authority.
GDPR applies to customer notes; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: How much of the catalogue has reliable compatibility attributes.
Which recommendations require specialist approval.
Freshness and reliability of price and availability data.
Whether the clerk has authority and training to serve occasional customers directly.
Applicable employee consultation and access requirements.
research_questions: Which explicit constraints eliminate unsuitable options without a model?
Can experienced clerks verify recommendation briefs quickly against approved sources?
Which recommendation errors require escalation rather than a revised draft?
new_work: Review recommendation briefs and confirm conversation outcomes.
Maintain suitability filters, source documents and escalation boundaries.
Check samples for unsupported claims and outdated product facts.
Train clerks to recognise technical limits and record unresolved needs.

tasks.short: Inspect outgoing work against customer specifications and resolve discrepancies before release.

steps.what: Retrieve the approved customer specification and outgoing work documents.
Compare outgoing item codes, quantities and recorded attributes with the approved order.
Inspect outgoing goods for condition, finish, labels and customer-specific requirements.
Record discrepancies and recommend correction, acceptance or a dispatch hold.
Approve release or hold the outgoing work for correction.

tasks.design: An integration assembles the current specification and dispatch records from the {DOCS}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. Deterministic checks compare recorded attributes and prefill an inspection checklist in the {OPS_SYSTEM}; people inspect physical work and judge discrepancies. The dispatch supervisor approves release, with findings and corrections retained against the order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications, dispatch records and inspection evidence were separate, while physical inspection could not be replaced by document checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and checklist generators can now be built more cheaply. Existing structured attributes support deterministic comparison without requiring automated visual inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Surface defects, bespoke finishes, ambiguous tolerances and unrecorded changes still require physical assessment and specialist judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a defect or mismatch that passes the recorded checks and deciding its practical significance.

ambition.what: Review recurring specification mismatches weekly with the sales supervisor.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling paperwork and more time inspecting work and documenting consequential discrepancies. Dispatch approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Prevent repeat order errors caused by unclear customer promises.
reach.learn: Translate inspection findings into precise order-entry requirements and customer acceptance criteria.

reach.task: Clarify technical acceptance criteria before an order is fulfilled.
reach.learn: Distinguish measurable tolerances from subjective preferences and identify authoritative specification versions.

evidence.claim: Order software can synchronise order and stock records; this does not establish physical inspection automation.
Recorded item codes, quantities and explicit tolerances can be compared deterministically.
Physical condition and ambiguous customer acceptance criteria commonly require human inspection.

assumptions: This version describes a merchandise business where the order clerk inspects outgoing goods.
Physical inspection takes more time than the supplied document-heavy prior suggests.
A dispatch supervisor currently approves release; local authority arrangements may differ.
Only approved structured criteria generate automatic checks; novel free-text requirements receive human interpretation.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer and employee records; consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Whether outgoing work consists of goods, service deliverables or advertising proofs.
Who performs physical inspection and who has release authority.
Which specification attributes and tolerances are structured.
How specification revisions and customer-approved deviations are recorded.
Whether suitable checklists already exist in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Access lead times and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which checks compare records, and which require observing the actual outgoing work?
Can the authoritative specification version be linked reliably to each dispatch?
Which discrepancy types recur and could be prevented during order intake?
new_work: Maintain checklist templates and approved tolerance rules.
Translate new customer-specific conditions into inspection criteria.
Resolve missing or conflicting specification versions.
Review comparison failures and maintain integration mappings.
Complete employee consultation where national rules require it.

role.altitude: The order clerk moves from transcription and document chasing toward resolving order exceptions, explaining options and verifying customer requirements. Commercial commitments, customer master-data changes and dispatch approval remain subject to explicit delegated authority.
reach: New accounts clerk: resolve customer identity and billing-data exceptions.
Account representative: turn documented customer needs into useful commercial follow-up.
Sales engineer: recognise technical limits and define acceptance criteria.
Sales supervisor: use recurring intake and inspection findings to prevent repeat errors.
skills_to_grow: Writing clear requirements and acceptance criteria.
Checking extracted fields against source documents.
Explaining product trade-offs and recognising escalation needs.
Maintaining workflow rules and handling integration failures.
role.ambitious_version: An order operations specialist who combines reliable intake, informed customer guidance and feedback from outgoing inspections, with explicitly delegated authority over standard order exceptions.
